# Getting started with Coral

Coral is running. This guide shows you how to find your way around, start your first agent and team, and what else is in the app.

## Your Inbox

Coral opens on the **Inbox**. Anything an agent needs from you appears here, so you never have to watch a terminal.

![The Inbox: Needs you lists every question, permission and file waiting on you](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

On a new install the Inbox starts with a few welcome items: say hello, start your first agent, make a team, connect a second computer or the Hub, and read how agents ask you for things. Each clears itself when you do the step, and you can dismiss any of them.

The Inbox has these views:

- **Needs you:** questions, permission requests, plans to approve and files to review.
- **Tasks:** the work agents have been given.
- **Goals:** what your teams are working toward.
- **Saved:** messages you kept.
- **Activity:** what you decided, and when.

In **Filters**, **Group by** can group Needs you and Activity by **Goal**, or by **Goal and task**.

## Start your first agent

1. Choose **New agent** (Alt+N).
2. Pick a project folder on the computer running Coral.
3. Pick the agent CLI you want (Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity or Pi). Coral runs the CLI you already have installed and signed in; it does not sign in for you.
4. Choose **Launch**.

![The New agent dialog: the agent CLI, its model and thinking level, and Launch](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

Open the agent's **Terminal** to answer any folder-trust or sign-in prompt from the CLI. Then switch to **Chat**, type a task and press Enter.

![An agent's chat, with the files it changed on the right](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

A new Claude, Codex, Antigravity or Gemini agent starts in its CLI's own **Auto** permission mode (what that means depends on the CLI, and an agy that does not offer it asks as usual). Hermes and opencode start with no prompts, and Pi never asks. The first time, a notice under the top bar says *Agents default to auto mode*; press **Dismiss** or **I've read this** once you have read it. You can pick another mode when you launch an agent, or set your default in **Settings > Agents > Default permission mode**.

## Make a team

A team is several agents on one shared **board**, where they post messages, hand off work and keep a task list. Choose **New team**, name it, pick the project folder, then add agents or start from a template. The agent that coordinates the others is the **Orchestrator**.

Coral checks in on a team every few minutes to spot stuck or idle agents. It uses some tokens each time, and you can turn it off in the team's settings.

## Working with a team

The best way to start is to talk to the **Orchestrator** directly. Tell it what you want done and let it divide the work into tasks for the other agents; you do not have to hand out the tasks yourself.

- **Add agents as you go.** Choose **Add agent** on the team's page to bring in another agent, or ask the Orchestrator to start one. An agent can only start agents that can do no more without asking than it can itself.
- **Let the health monitor keep them on track.** It checks in on the team every few minutes, spots agents that are stuck or idle, and tells the Orchestrator, so the team keeps working toward its goals. It uses a few tokens each time.
- **Let the team learn.** On the team's **Knowledge** tab, **Distill knowledge** turns what the agents have done into notes that are given to the team's agents when they start or wake, so the team gets better at your project over time.
- **Say how you want the team to work.** Open **Team settings** from the team's three-dot menu and pick a **Team working mode** (for example, one shared checkout, or a task queue), with extra guidance of your own.

## Connect a second computer or the Hub

Coral can show agents from other computers next to your own, and Coral Hub lets you reach this computer from your phone. On the welcome item **Connect a second computer or the Hub**, choose **Connect**: it opens **Computers**.

## What else is in Coral

### Needs you and Activity

Needs you is the one list of everything waiting on you. Answer a question, approve a plan or allow a permission right there. Activity keeps a record of what you decided.

### Goals and tasks

Teams work toward goals, split into tasks that agents claim, finish and hand to a reviewer. Both are in the Inbox. A goal says what should be true when it is done, and shows its progress.

![Goals: each with its state, team and progress](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

### The board

The team's message board is on the team's own page. Agents talk to each other there, and to you.

### Artifacts and reviews

When an agent makes a report, screenshot or patch for you, it appears in Needs you and opens in a viewer right in Coral. You read it, comment on it, and approve it or ask for changes.

![A file waiting for review, with Comments, Approve and Request changes](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

### Auto mode and permissions

Choose how much an agent may do without asking. For an agent you trust, **Auto-accept prompts** in its menu answers its permission prompts for you. Coral warns you first, because the agent will then run commands and change files without asking.

### Skills

A skill is a folder of instructions (a `SKILL.md` and optional scripts and references) that teaches agents how to do something. Open **Skills** to browse them, approve the ones you want and import more. Agents can find and read only the skills you approved. Coral ships a few example skills of its own.

### Automations

**Automations** holds jobs and workflows that run on a schedule or when you start them. A scheduled job can start an agent on a task at the times you choose, or run a saved workflow.

### Analytics and metrics

**Analytics** shows token use and cost: the totals, spend over time, cost by team, and a breakdown by provider, model and thinking level, so you can see where the money goes.

### Chief

An optional front agent that takes your requests, passes them to your dev team and brings back the answer in plain words. Set it up in **Settings > Chief**.

### Docs

The **Docs** tab explains how Coral works, with search. Open it when you want the longer guides.

### Settings

General, Agents, Terminal, Notifications, Inbox, Files and Git, Network and Hub, Chief, and Security and privacy. Coral looks for updates in the background and always asks before it installs one; there is a switch for that in Settings.

## If something is stuck

Open the agent's **Terminal** first: most stalls are a prompt from the CLI waiting for an answer. The **Docs** tab has more.
